terms.definition: The property of matter that makes particles attract or repel electrically.
terms.function: The spark behind force, current, and static cling.
terms.whereItIs: The two balls on the bench.
terms.whyItMatters: Without charge there is no electricity at all.

terms.definition: The rule that same-sign charges push apart and opposite signs pull together.
terms.whyItMatters: It predicts every force between charged objects, from balloons to lightning.
terms.whereItIs: The force arrows between the balls.

terms.definition: The way negative electrons shift between objects (rubbing, wires, sparks).
terms.whyItMatters: It explains how rubbing makes static and how current flows at all.

terms.definition: The build-up of unbalanced charge on an object, waiting to rebalance.
terms.whyItMatters: It's the energy behind shock, cling, and zaps — and the tension the spark relieves.
terms.whereItIs: The bench before the spark rail fires.
